page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r5.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual server hosted on the KVM hypervisor. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it is powered by an Intel Xeon 8163 processor operating at a base frequency of 2.5 GHz. The instance configuration allocates 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with hyper-threading enabled. It includes 32 GB of RAM, establishing an 8-to-1 memory-to-vCPU ratio (8 GB per vCPU). The processor supports advanced instruction sets including AVX, AVX-512, and AES-NI. No local NVMe or SSD storage is bundled with this instance type, requiring external cloud storage volumes, and baseline network throughput is provisioned at 2 Gbps.

Across empirical benchmark tests, the ecs.r5.xlarge demonstrates entry-level performance metrics relative to contemporary cloud hardware. Its single-core and multi-core processing scores place it in the bottom 25 percent of tested virtual machines in both stress-ng and Geekbench evaluations. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reaches 20.9 GB/sec and write bandwidth measures 18.67 GB/sec, reflecting lower-tier throughput for memory operations. The instance demonstrates consistent throughput for Redis SET operations at 2.85 million operations per second and handles lightweight LLM inference on small models, though it exhibits significant latency on compute-heavy compression and text processing suites.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.r5.xlarge provides access to a large memory allocation without demanding investment in higher core counts. Because compute-per-core and uncached memory bandwidth fall into lower comparative percentiles, this configuration represents a clear tradeoff prioritizing capacity over raw throughput. It is most suitable for memory-sensitive enterprise tasks that do not depend on intense compute cycles, such as in-memory data caching, staging or development database environments, and lightweight web or microservice application layers.

It is equipped with 32 GB of system memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU memory allocation ratio suited for memory-intensive applications. The instance is primarily suited for in-memory caching solutions such as Redis, moderate relational databases, and background memory-heavy business services.
